description: Simplify the demo gripper (cad/openscad/demo_gripper) and align the hardware with the 'mirror a human' principle. (1) The current design looks bulky. Slim it down and simplify it: fewer, smaller parts, less material, with the same interchangeable-jaw interface. Stay in OpenSCAD (Jake prefers it: open source). (2) Remove the camera attachment/bracket from the gripper. (3) Vision: the only cameras are two binocular (stereo) cameras mounted roughly where a human's eyes are. No wrist or gripper cameras. (4) Any sensing on the gripper itself would be 'four sensors' (Jake's words; likely force sensors in the fingertips, i.e. touch, which fits the human analogy; confirm with Jake and leave room for them without designing them in yet). Record the principle in the plans (update plans/hand_1_0.md and any camera assumptions elsewhere): mirror how a human perceives and uses things. Render before/after views for Jake.

results.identified_issue: Generalist's device geometry is unpublished (press says 'UMI-style pincers'/'Data Hands'); interpreted as UMI fin-ray look, same reading the repo's hand_gripper already used ('lattice fingers that curve in to a point'). gen_01 reuses hand_gripper.scad modules via use<> exactly like gen_00 (hub(), jaw_link2d, gear_sector2d, so101_mount untouched). gen_00 = git mv of demo_gripper.scad, content unchanged; exported STLs byte-identical to previous. export.py: discovers gen_[0-9][0-9]_*.scad, PARTS rows may have 6 cols [piece,name,color,explode,material,bed]; 4-col rows (gen_00) default to PLA and bed=a_/b_ prefix. Optional '// label:' line names a generation. Stale export/render files from the old flat layout are deleted by export.py. parts.json gains 'generations':[{id,label,source}] and per-part material+group; stage_cad_models.py passes them through (assembly_groups) — single-generation designs behave as before. App: CADPart.material/group, CADDesign.groups; AssemblyScene lays groups along X by measured bounds (assembled ∪ exploded) + 50 mm gap, SCNText billboard labels, resetCamera(group:) for chips; head-on camera for 'All' when >1 group. Verified: swiftc -typecheck for macOS + iOS, and an offscreen SCNRenderer snapshot of AssemblyScene on macOS (no app build per rules). validate.py now loops generations; gen_01 'clash' also checks finger∩root empty. Unverified: TPU tongue fit, fin-ray stiffness, real phone UI (chip bar overlay over SceneView gestures).
results.summary: Added gen_01 with Generalist/UMI-style TPU fin-ray fingers, made every design pass a numbered gen file, and the app now lines the generations up side by side with labels.
results.detailed_description:
New generation: gen_01 · fin-ray TPU fingers. Each jaw is now two prints. A stiff PETG root keeps the same gears, pivot and arm mount, plus the strap slot your finger presses on. A long TPU 95A finger slides over a tongue on the root and is held by one M3 bolt. The finger is a fin-ray: thin walls joined by slanted ribs, so when it presses an object the gripping face wraps around it. That's the soft-fingertip part of the human analogy, so no grip tape is needed. Tips reach 108 mm (gen_00 was 72). Materials: fingers are TPU, the roots, hub and arm cradle are PETG, and the small pivot insert is PLA. The README has a table of this per generation.

About 'look like Generalist': they haven't published their gripper's geometry. The press only calls it 'UMI-style pincers', so I went with the UMI look: long, slim fingers that curve in to a point. If you have a photo of the exact gripper you mean, send it and gen_02 will copy it more closely.

Generations: the old file is now gen_00_slim_two_pairs.scad, unchanged (it exports byte-identical meshes). The new one is gen_01_finray_tpu.scad, a copy that was then changed. The rule is in the README and the file header: copy the newest file to the next number, never edit an older one. export.py picks up every gen_NN file automatically. Each generation gets its own print-ready zip and renders, plus render/generations.png with all of them side by side.

App: the 3D view puts every generation in a row, oldest on the left, each with a floating label. Chips along the top (All / gen_00 / gen_01) frame one generation at a time. Assemble/Explode still works and moves every generation's pieces. The parts list is grouped by generation and shows each part's material. The picture is the CAD in-hand comparison next to the app's own scene code rendered offscreen on the Mac. I didn't run it on the phone, since Vigil does that build.

Checks: 106 clearance and gear checks pass across both generations, and all 14 meshes are watertight single solids. Nothing is printed or hand-tested yet. The TPU-to-PETG tongue fit (0.2 mm clearance) is the first thing to check on a test print.
results.user_reply_draft: Thanks Jake. There's a new version of the gripper with long, soft TPU fingers in the Generalist/UMI style. They bend around whatever they grip, like a fingertip would. Every version is now saved as its own numbered file, so nothing gets overwritten. The app shows them all in a row with labels, and you can tap to jump between them. Explode and assemble still work on every version. If you have a photo of the exact Generalist gripper you mean, send it over and the next version will follow it more closely.

results.notes: More from Jake: (1) Make it look much more like Generalist Robotics' gripper. (2) Design with TPU printing in mind where it helps (e.g. compliant fingertips or flexures), noting which parts are TPU and which are PLA/PETG. (3) Keep every iteration: each generation is a NEW file (copy the previous one, then change it), labeled, e.g. cad/openscad/demo_gripper/gen_01_<label>.scad, gen_02_<label>.scad. Never overwrite an earlier generation. Keep the current design as gen_00. (4) In the phone app's 3D view, show all generations lined up side by side, each labeled, so Jake can scroll through them. Keep the existing explode/assemble feature (Jake really likes it) working for every generation.

results.identified_issue: Jaws: pad depth 18->10 mm, widths 24/32->16/22 mm, outer finger saddle sphere removed (digit presses on flat back of jaw under the strap), strap slot moved to x=pad_depth-5. Hub: hand_gripper hub() intersected with a rounded hull of pivot circles + bridge-bolt bosses, so every inherited hole, the nut trap and the cheek planes stay put and so101_mount/pivot_insert/servo envelope are unchanged (fitclash/insertclash/clash all still pass). I deliberately did NOT edit ../hand_gripper/hand_gripper.scad (older design still uses it) and did not touch so101_mount (29.6 cm3, the bulkiest piece, but its size is set by the UNMEASURED STS3215 envelope). camera part, check_camera.py and camera_check.txt deleted; validate.py now expects 7 parts. validate.py: 70 collision/positive-control cases pass, all 7 meshes watertight single solids, 4 jaws bed-oriented. Volumes: A pair 42.1->22.2 cm3; handheld kit A ~75->43 cm3. 'Four sensors' interpreted as two per jaw fingertip force/touch: sensor_pockets=false param cuts 2x 12x8x1.2 mm seats per face + lead channel when true (renders without warnings, not exported). Plans: hand_1_0.md gets a 'Principle: mirror a human' section and a rewritten §3 (stereo pair at eye height, worn by demonstrator / head-mounted on robot), plus umbilical, BOM and open-question edits; handheld_gripper.md and crow_gripper.md got superseding banners rather than full rewrites. Before/after image built from the previous scad (copied to scratch before editing) at identical gimbal cameras, composed with PIL. Not verified: printing, fit in hand, whether head cameras can see the contact patch past the hand.
results.summary: Slimmed the OpenSCAD demo gripper, removed its camera bracket, and wrote the mirror-a-human principle into the plans.
results.detailed_description:
The gripper is lighter and simpler: seven parts instead of eight, and the handheld kit uses about 43 cm³ of plastic instead of 75. Each jaw is now 10 mm deep (was 18) and 16 / 22 mm wide (was 24 / 32), the bulky finger saddles are gone, and your finger pad presses straight on the flat back of the jaw under the strap. The hub keeps every hole but is trimmed to a rounded shape. The jaw interface, gears, servo cradle and arm mount are unchanged, and all 70 clearance checks still pass.

The camera bracket and its ray-check script are deleted. The plans now say the only cameras are a stereo pair at eye height: worn by you when demonstrating, mounted at head height on the robot. That's a new "Mirror a human" section and a rewritten camera section in plans/hand_1_0.md, with notes in the handheld and crow plans pointing to it.

For the four sensors I assumed fingertip touch, two per jaw. There's a switch (sensor_pockets) that cuts four small seats in the gripping faces, but it's off, so nothing is designed in yet. Is fingertip touch what you meant? Before/after is in plans/demo_gripper_before_after.png.
results.user_reply_draft: Thanks Jake. I slimmed the gripper down a lot: thinner, narrower jaws, a rounder hub, and the camera bracket is gone, so it's about 40% less plastic with the same swappable jaws. The plans now say the only cameras are two stereo 'eyes' at head height, and there's room in the fingertips for four touch sensors. Can you confirm touch is what you meant by the four sensors?

user_request.name: I definitely prefer OpenSCAD since it's open source. I don't know if I like the current design, it looks a little bulky. Could we simplify it? We don't need to worry about the camera attachment. The only cameras would be two binocular cameras near where humans' eyes are. I don't think we want extra cameras. If we need sensors on the device themselves, there'll be four sensors. We really want to mirror how a human would use things.

summary: The demo gripper should look much more like Generalist Robotics' gripper, use TPU where it helps (compliant fingertips or flexures), and mark each part as TPU or PLA/PETG. Each design iteration must be a new labeled file (gen_00 is the current design, then gen_01_<label>.scad and so on), and the phone app's 3D view must show every generation side by side, labeled, with explode/assemble working on each.
